title: Separate permission from a portal error
summary: If ERP shows an error, save the exact error and what you were trying to do. If the screen works but you're unsure whether you're allowed to apply, put that question first when you contact the Academic Section.

title: Keep the notice and your attempt together
summary: Save the current notice, a screenshot of any error, and when you tried to register. Put the course code and admission batch in the same message so the office can identify the notice you mean.

title: Ask one clear question after a missed window
summary: Mention when you saw the notice and ask whether there is a late request route for your batch. If you get a verbal answer, make a quick note of what to do next and who to follow up with.

title: Keep your payment reference handy
summary: If an amount was already debited, note the transaction reference and the status shown in ERP before asking support what happened. Share only the details the office needs, never your PIN or OTP.

title: Find the assessment behind the grade
summary: Check whether the concern is a marking error, a missing assessment, or a grade you want explained. Pick one and point to the entry or question you want the instructor to review.

title: Make comparisons easy to check
summary: If two places show different marks, note both values, where each appears, and the assessment date. Ask the instructor which record to use.

title: Ask for feedback you can act on
summary: If you're mainly worried about a low grade, ask which part of the assessment cost marks and whether you can view the evaluated work. Keep the first message focused on understanding the result.

title: Keep a copy of what you asked
summary: Write down the assessment, the question you raised and the response. If you need to follow up, you can refer to the earlier answer without explaining the entire case again.

title: Ask for a viewing slot
summary: Put the course code and mid-sem assessment in the subject. Ask when and where you can view the script and whether you need to bring anything.

title: Pick the questions before you go
summary: Write down the question numbers you want to discuss, especially if you noticed an unmarked page or a possible totalling error.

title: Ask about another slot if there’s a clash
summary: If you have a lab or exam during the viewing time, tell the instructor what clashes and ask what alternative arrangements are available.

title: Check the announcement channel
summary: Look at recent course announcements before sending a second message. If you find a viewing announcement, refer to it when asking the instructor about your case.

title: Start with the clearest discrepancy
summary: Write one sentence describing the specific error you think occurred and where you spotted it. Include the course code and ask the instructor to check that discrepancy.

title: Write down the answer you need
summary: Ask the instructor whether a change is possible. If they refer you to the Academic Section, ask which procedure and deadline apply to your admission batch.

title: Keep earlier replies on the same thread
summary: When following up on a grade issue, keep the original thread and the assessment reference. A short recap of what the instructor checked can save the next office time.

title: Flag a real dependency
summary: If the result affects another registration or a time-sensitive application, say what depends on it. Ask which part of the review you can complete while waiting.

title: Make a course-by-course list
summary: Separate the affected dates by course and note any lab or assessment you missed. Bring that list when you ask your advisor what applies.

title: Confirm where documents belong
summary: Keep relevant records ready and ask the designated office which documents it needs and which channel to use. Keep sensitive medical details out of class groups.

title: Check whether the record itself is wrong
summary: If you attended and the record shows an absence, start with the specific class and date. Ask the instructor to check the entry before you look into a waiver.

title: Ask about compensating work
summary: If you missed graded work as well as class, put both concerns on your list. Ask separately what you can do about the lab or assessment.

title: Forward the first message
summary: When you follow up with the department office, keep the original subject line and thread. Add one sentence saying what decision you need and include any relevant deadline.

title: Ask who can take it up
summary: If your advisor is unavailable, ask the office who is covering the issue and which inbox to use. Mention which course and batch the request concerns.

title: Track what you’ve already tried
summary: Keep a short list of when you emailed, who replied, and what they suggested. You can share that recap if another person picks up the issue.

title: Give context before walking over
summary: If a visit would help, call or email to confirm who handles the issue and when they're available. Take your course details and the earlier correspondence.
